description: Figures what a business deduction saves a self-employed person in 2026 or 2027 (tax_year; 2027 on the IRS's published 2027 amounts, federal only, a dollar deduction since the 2027 mileage rate is not published): 2026 business miles split at July 1 (72.5 and 76 cents a mile) or a dollar expense, off the Schedule C profit, and the income tax, self-employment tax, earned income credit and state tax saved, from the federal return and the state return at the profit and at the profit less the deduction (the half-SE-tax and qualified business income deductions move with it). Ohio and Pennsylvania state tax are not computed. Returns each saving, the total and every default assumed. Computed by QuantCalc's federal and state tax APIs, the engines the website's IRS mileage rate page is checked against to the cent. Requires a connected QuantCalc PRO licence or Tax Season Pass; without one it returns no figures and names the free web calculator. Not tax advice.

age.description: The filer's age in the tax year (16-110). Default 40 (under 65), as the website's calculator takes it.

business_miles_after_july.description: Business miles driven July 1 to December 31, 2026 (76 cents a mile).

business_miles_before_july.description: Business miles driven January 1 to June 30, 2026 (72.5 cents a mile). Give miles or deduction_amount, not both.

deduction_amount.description: The business deduction in dollars, instead of miles (any Schedule C expense).

filing_status.description: Filing status: single, married filing jointly (mfj), married filing separately (mfs) or head of household (hoh).

net_profit.description: The Schedule C net profit for the tax year BEFORE this deduction (more than 0).

other_wages.description: Other household income as W-2 wages: the filer's own, on a joint return the spouse's. Default 0.

spouse_age.description: Joint return only: the spouse's age in the tax year. Default: the same as age.

state.description: Optional two-letter state of residence, or DC: adds the 2026 state tax saving (none for 2027: the state API's self-employment path files its own 2026 federal return). Ohio and Pennsylvania are not computed (their own rules for business income).

tax_year.description: The tax year: 2026 (default) or 2027. 2027: the federal income and self-employment tax on the IRS's published 2027 amounts (Rev. Proc. 2026-35) and SSA's 2027 wage base; the 2027 mileage rate is not published yet, so 2027 takes deduction_amount, not miles; no state saving for 2027. Stated in the result.

name: business_deduction_tax_savings
title: Tax saved by a self-employed business deduction (2026 or 2027)
